---
title: "Session 0: Setup and orientation"
subtitle: "Required self-study diagnostic"
---

Session 0 is completed before the first class. Its purpose is to find installation
problems early, not to test prior programming knowledge.

## Learning goals

After completing the diagnostic, you should be able to:

- Start RStudio and identify the console and source editor.
- Run an R expression and save instructions in a source file.
- Open an RStudio project.
- Create and render a Quarto document to HTML.
- Locate the source file and the rendered output.
- Copy an error message when asking for help.

## Install in this order

Use only the official links below. You do not need to install any R packages,
GitHub Desktop, or a separate Git graphical interface.

### 1. Install R

R is the program that performs the calculations. Choose your operating system
from the official [R download page](https://cran.r-project.org/):

- **Windows:** [Download R for Windows](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)
- **macOS:** [Download R for macOS](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/)

Accept the standard installation options. If R is already installed, you do not
need to reinstall it merely to complete this diagnostic.

### 2. Install RStudio Desktop

RStudio is the interface we will use during the opening sessions. Download the
free, open-source edition from the official
[RStudio Desktop download page](https://posit.co/downloads/).

Install **R before RStudio**. Then start RStudio once and confirm that the Console
opens without an error.

### 3. Verify Quarto

Quarto turns a source document containing prose and R code into an HTML report.
First try the rendering exercise below. If RStudio cannot render a `.qmd` file,
use the official [Quarto installation page](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)
and then restart RStudio.

### 4. Install Git using the course recommendation

Git records versions of analytical source files. We will use command-line Git
through RStudio's **Terminal** tab; we will not require GitHub Desktop.

#### Windows

1. Download [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/install/windows).
2. Choose the standard 64-bit installer unless you know that your computer uses
   Windows on ARM.
3. Accept the installer defaults.
4. Completely close and reopen RStudio after installation.

#### macOS

1. Open **Terminal**.
2. Run:

   ```bash
   git --version
   ```

3. If macOS offers to install the Command Line Developer Tools, accept the
   installation. If no prompt appears and Git is unavailable, run:

   ```bash
   xcode-select --install
   ```

See the official [Git installation instructions for macOS](https://git-scm.com/install/mac).

#### Linux

Use the Git package supplied by your Linux distribution. See the official
[Git installation page](https://git-scm.com/install/linux).

### 5. Verify Git inside RStudio

After restarting RStudio, select **Tools → Terminal → New Terminal** and run:

```bash
git --version
```

A successful result begins with `git version`. You do not need to create a GitHub
account or configure GitHub authentication yet; that will happen before Session 2.

::: {.callout-tip}
## If your computer requires administrator approval

Do not download an installer from an unofficial mirror. Submit the error or
permission message and contact the course TA while there is still time to resolve
the installation.
:::

## Part 1: Verify R

Open RStudio and run these expressions in the console:

```r
R.version.string
2 + 3
mean(c(4, 7, 9))
```

You should see an R version, the value `5`, and the value `6.666667`.

## Part 2: Distinguish console from source

Create a new R script and save it as `setup-check.R`. Add:

```r
measurements <- c(4, 7, 9)
mean_measurement <- mean(measurements)
mean_measurement
```

Run the script one line at a time. Close and reopen the file. The source remains;
the console output is not the analytical record.

## Part 3: Open the project

In your local course repository, open `course/session00/`. Copy
`BIOS6301-setup.Rproj` and `diagnostic-starter.qmd` into a new folder named
`BIOS6301-setup`, then open the copied `.Rproj` file.

Confirm that the project name appears in the upper-right corner of RStudio.

## Part 4: Render a Quarto document

Open the copied `diagnostic-starter.qmd` and render it to HTML.

The document passes when:

- `diagnostic-starter.html` is created.
- The HTML contains the value `6.7`.
- The HTML contains a small scatterplot.
- The Git check reports a line beginning with `git version`.
- No error appears during rendering.


## How to ask for help

Include all four items:

1. Your operating system
2. `R.version.string`
3. What you clicked or ran
4. The complete error message as text

Screenshots can supplement the error message but should not replace copied text.
